title: POC scoping - episodic bursts & token exchange - CycloneAI
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week POC to validate CycloneAI's episodic burst use case. Discussed steady vs burst QPS, concurrency, token length skew (few long responses), benchmark methodology (replay + synthetic bursts), security requirements (SOC2, SSO, KMS), and acceptance criteria (95th pct latency, cost per 1k tokens). Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, access instructions, pricing estimate, schedule first replay run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-11-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood SE), Priya (CycloneAI CTO), Marcus (Eng Lead), Sofia (SRE), Amin (Product)

Summary auto: POC scoping for bursty traffic profile, focus on tail latency and cost controls, run replay + synthetic-burst benchmark, 6 week timeline

00:00 Maya: okay, thanks everyone for joining, um we'll run through objectives and then dig into the traffic shape, so quick intros?
00:15 Priya: hi I'm Priya, CTO at CycloneAI, we build an augmented analytics assistant used in realtime customer support, our main ask is we get, like, spikes during major incidents and we care about tail latency.
00:32 Marcus: Marcus here, lead on infra, we own the infra and the replay dataset.
00:39 Sofia: Sofia, SRE, I'll be running the load playbacks and validating SLOs.
:44 Maya: great, Diego and Leah are our SEs, Diego will drive the workload sizing conversation.
00:52 Diego: cool, thanks. quick agenda: success criteria, traffic numbers (qps/concurrency), token stats, benchmark plan, security checklist, timeline.
01:05 Amin: timeline is important for us, target is to have production decision in 6-8 weeks.
01:12 Leah: noted. success criteria - what would make the POC a win for CycloneAI?
01:20 Priya: three things: one, 95th percentile latency under 300ms for short queries; two, predictable cost per 1k tokens compared to our current self-hosted infra; three, smooth failover to hosted fallback if our dedicated pool is saturated.
01:38 Diego: good. quick clarifying q: by short queries you mean input+output tokens under 500 total?
01:44 Priya: yes, typical short is < 450 tokens, but beware we have a long-tail — about 2-3% of requests generate multi-turn transcripts of 1200 tokens out.
02:00 Marcus: to add, our steady qps is around 60 qps, with episodic bursts up to 420 qps for 3-12 minute windows during incidents — those are the pain points.
02:16 Diego: okay that's helpful. do you have concurrency numbers?
02:19 Marcus: concurrency typically 40-80 during bursts, but normally around 15.
02:27 Diego: perfect. so we should model both the sustained 24h profile and short high amplitude bursts.
02:34 Maya: also important: token distribution — what's the median input length, median output length?
02:40 Priya: median input ~35 tokens, median output ~120 tokens. but mean output is skewed by long transcripts, mean ~340 tokens.
02:50 Leah: that's a big skew. for benchmarking we need to capture that 95th and 99th token lengths. do you have histograms?
03:00 Marcus: yes, we'll share a 7-day histogram export, includes percentiles and a sample of large responses.
03:06 Diego: great. quick note on models — do you plan to use a single model family or mix smaller fast models for short queries and larger ones for longform?
03:16 Priya: mixed. On normal queries we want a cost-efficient 7B-ish model, but for some escalation paths we invoke a 30B variant. so the POC needs to show routing behavior.
03:26 Diego: that adds complexity — we can simulate model-variant routing in the benchmark, Redwood supports policy-based routing and fallback to hosted model variants.
03:35 Sofia: on security, we need SOC2, SSO/SAML for user access, and KMS-backed key management for any private deploy. Also audit logs retention 12 months.
03:46 Leah: we have an enterprise pack that covers SOC2 docs and KMS integrations, we'll attach that to the workspace.
03:52 Priya: for private data handling we need to keep all logs in our VPC for the pilot. is that doable?
04:00 Maya: yes, Redwood Private can run in your VPC or we can provide a private control plane; we'll detail options in the security packet.
04:09 Diego: switching back to numbers — Marcus said steady 60 qps and peaks 420, concurrency 40-80. for bench we recommend a 24 hour replay at your live mix, then run 5 synthetic burst tests: 1x 5min at 420 qps, 1x 10min at 300 qps, and a staircase load to capture tail behavior.
04:31 Marcus: timeline for running those?
04:34 Diego: with access to your replay traces and API keys, we can run initial replay within 72 hours on our infra, then iterate with optimizations.
04:41 Maya: POC phases: week 0-1 onboarding and test config, week 2 baseline replay, week 3 burst runs and profiling, week 4 perf tuning (batching, cache), week 5 security & compliance review, week 6 final analysis and decision.
04:58 Priya: that's tight but works. cost expectations?
05:03 Diego: we'll provide an estimated cost-per-token model for hosted vs dedicated. approximate numbers during POC will be indicative; final numbers depend on configured batching and quantization.
05:15 Marcus: we use KV cache heavily in prod — we need to ensure token-level caching is preserved; heard you have prefix/KV cache, but sometimes that term is transcribed as 'kay vee cache' in other notes.
05:27 Leah: yes, we support KV cache and prefix caching; in benchmarking we'll toggle cache on/off to measure delta.
05:34 Sofia: also need to know fallback behavior for capacity: if dedicated pool is full does Redwood auto-fall back to hosted and what are data residency implications?
05:44 Maya: policy-driven routing — you can set fallbacks to hosted with or without sending raw payloads; for privacy-sensitive paths we can route to private only and return throttles vs fallback. we'll document options.
05:57 Priya: for acceptance we want a clear pass/fail criteria: 95th pct latency < 300ms for short queries during bursts and cost delta < 20% vs our expected baseline.
06:10 Diego: we'll capture those metrics; we'll also collect 99th and the error rates under burst.
06:16 Marcus: what about very long outputs (the 2-3% you mentioned)? they tend to push memory/kv usage.
06:22 Diego: for long outputs we recommend quantized model variants and possibly batching configs that avoid long-response head-of-line blocking — we'll show options in the tuning phase.
06:33 Leah: one practical ask — provide a small sample harness for running a replay locally so your team can sanity check before we kick off on our infra.
06:42 Marcus: yes we can run the harness.
06:45 Amin: can we get the benchmark template and a sample results dashboard?
06:49 Maya: yes we'll send the benchmark YAML and a sample dashboard; it's usually a Grafana snapshot + CSV of token latency buckets.
06:58 Diego: also to note, we measure latencies in two ways: end-to-end (client-to-response) and server-token-latency (strictly inference). both matter for SLOs.
07:09 Priya: do you collect per-token cost breakdowns? we want token-level accounting to tie back to our billing.
07:15 Diego: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdown and route-by-model costs.
07:22 Sofia: any limitations on concurrency per GPU? we need to ensure your dedicated pools map to our QPS needs.
07:28 Diego: we'll recommend pool sizing based on tokens/sec not just qps; a single GPU can handle more short-turn qps than longform. we'll produce a sizing table.
07:37 Marcus: alright let's talk data for replay — we'll provide a parquet export with fields: request_id, timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, model_variant_flag, metadata.
07:49 Leah: that's perfect. include a flag for 'escalation' so we can route those to larger models in the simulation.
07:55 Marcus: will do.
08:00 Maya: ok next, benchmarks and acceptance metrics recap — Diego?
08:05 Diego: baseline replay: run 24h at real mix -> collect 50/95/99 latencies, error rates, cost per 1k tokens. Synthetic bursts: run the five burst patterns to measure tail and queueing effects. For long response testing, run isolated high-output tests at 250 concurrent long responses. Acceptance: 95th < 300ms on short queries, error rate < 0.5% during bursts, and cost within 20% of baseline.
08:33 Priya: behavior during cache warmup is important — we'd like to see warmup profiles.
08:36 Diego: we'll capture prefix/KV cache warmup and show delta numbers.
08:40 Maya: who owns what next?
08:43 Marcus: we'll export the 7-day histograms and the parquet for replay by tomorrow EOD.
08:48 Priya: security contacts will review the enterprise pack once you share it. my security lead Jane will follow up.
08:54 Leah: we'll send the security packet and SOC2 artifacts, and a KMS integration guide.
08:59 Maya: our immediate deliverables: benchmark template, access instructions, pricing estimate, sample dashboard, security pack. we'll aim to send everything within 48 hours.
09:10 Amin: perfect. any competitors you think we'll compare?
09:13 Priya: we'll be looking at self-hosted GPU fleet cost and a managed provider named 'StratusAI' — small chance we'll also evaluate a big cloud custom endpoint.
09:24 Diego: noted, we'll include comparative notes.
09:28 Marcus: on instrumentation — do you require any SDK or is traffic replay via HTTP?
09:33 Leah: traffic replay is via HTTP to the same Redwood API endpoints; we provide a small replay client.
09:38 Sofia: monitoring hooks? we want metrics exported to our Prometheus stack.
09:42 Maya: we can emit metrics via Prometheus export or push to your Grafana Cloud.
09:48 Priya: any gotchas on RBAC or SSO?
09:51 Leah: support for SAML/SCIM and role-based access, we'll provide a setup guide.
09:55 Diego: about fallback data residency, quick note: if you choose to allow hosted fallback, payloads can be restricted to region — we support EU/US/APAC region pins.
10:05 Priya: ok sounds good. timeline reconfirm: we run onboarding this week, baseline replay next week, bursts the week after, tuning and security review weeks 3-4, final review week 6.
10:17 Maya: thanks. last quick clarifying q — for cost comparison, do you have an internal cost-per-1k token baseline?
10:23 Marcus: rough internal number is $0.80 per 1k tokens for our self-hosted when amortized; we want to see <= 20% delta for similar perf.
10:33 Diego: we'll model both per-token and per-concurrency economics.
10:37 Priya: any questions from your side?
10:40 Diego: none for now.
10:41 Maya: recap next steps and we'll capture action items.
10:44 Maya: action items: CycloneAI - share parquet + histograms (Marcus) by 2028-11-10, Redwood - send benchmark template + security pack (Maya/Leah) by 2028-11-11, Redwood - schedule baseline replay slot (Diego) for 2028-11-12, Redwood - pricing estimate (Maya) by 2028-11-11.
10:57 Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
11:00 Meeting ends
